<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>

% Grid dimensions
total_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_) }.
total_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_,C,_) }.

% Full row (a row where every column has the same non‑zero colour)
full_row(R,Vc) :- total_cols(M), #count{C : input(R,C,Vc)} = M,
                  #count{C : input(R,C,_) } = M, Vc != 0.

% Wall row (the unique full row; its colour is Vc)
wall_row(W,Vc) :- full_row(W,Vc), not full_row(R2,Vc2), R2 < W.

% Candidate source cells (non‑zero, not the wall colour)
candidate(R,C,V,D) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0,
                      wall_row(W,Vc), V != Vc,
                      R >= W,  D = R - W.
candidate(R,C,V,D) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0,
                      wall_row(W,Vc), V != Vc,
                      R <  W,  D = W - R.

% Minimal distance per column (the smallest D for that column)
col_min_dist(C,D) :- candidate(R,C,V,D),
                    #count{R2,V2 : candidate(R2,C,V2,D2), D2 < D} = 0.

% Max colour at that minimal distance for each column
col_max_colour(C,Vmax) :- col_min_dist(C,D),
                         candidate(R,C,Vmax,D),
                         #count{R2,V2 : candidate(R2,C,V2,D), V2 > Vmax} = 0.

% Global minimal distance (over all columns) and maximal colour among those
global_min_dist(G) :- col_min_dist(C,G),
                     #count{C2,D2 : col_min_dist(C2,D2), D2 < G} = 0.

max_colour_G(Vmax) :- global_min_dist(G),
                       col_max_colour(C,Vmax),
                       #count{C2,V2 : col_max_colour(C2,V2), col_min_dist(C2,G), V2 > Vmax} = 0.

% Source cell for each column (nearest with maximal colour at its minimal distance)
source(C,R,V) :- col_min_dist(C,D), col_max_colour(C,V), candidate(R,C,V,D).

% Column classifications
is_high(C,R,V)  :- source(C,R,V), global_min_dist(G), max_colour_G(Vmax), V = Vmax.
is_low (C,R,V)  :- source(C,R,V), global_min_dist(G), max_colour_G(Vmax), V < Vmax.

% Max row index
max_row(Rmax) :- total_rows(N), Rmax = N - 1.

% Cells filled by a HIGH column (full interval between source and wall)
high_fill(R,C,Vsrc) :- is_high(C,Rsrc,Vsrc), Rsrc < W, R = Rsrc+1,
                         R <= W-1, input(R,C,0), Vsrc = Color.
high_fill(R,C,Vsrc) :- is_high(C,Rsrc,Vsrc), Rsrc > W, R = W+1,
                         R = Rsrc-1, R <= max_row, input(R,C,0), Vsrc = Color.

% Cells filled by a LOW or OTHER column (single outward step)
step_fill(R,C,Vsrc) :- source(C,Rsrc,Vsrc), not is_high(C,Rsrc,Vsrc),
                       R = Rsrc-1, R >= 0, input(R,C,0), Vsrc = Color.
step_fill(R,C,Vsrc) :- source(C,Rsrc,Vsrc), not is_high(C,Rsrc,Vsrc),
                       Rsrc > W, R = Rsrc+1, R <= max_row,
                       input(R,C,0), Vsrc = Color.

expected(R,C,Color) :- is_wall(R,C,Color).
expected(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,Color), Color != 0, not is_wall(R,C,Color).
expected(R,C,Color) :- high_fill(R,C,Color).
step_fill(R,C,Color) :- expected(R,C,Color).   % ensures low/other cells are covered

% Wall predicate
is_wall(R,C,Color) :- full_row(R,Vc), R = W, Color = Vc, Vc != 0.

% Output – exactly one colour per cell and it must be the expected colour
output_cell(R,C) :- true.
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color), expected(R,C,Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Transformation rule for the given examples
%  -------------------------------------------------
%
%  1. The whole grid contains a “wall” – a row that is filled
%     with the same non‑zero colour (the value 5 in the examples).
%     The wall splits the grid into an upper part (rows < wall) and a
%     lower part (rows > wall).  All non‑zero cells (value != 5) are
%     sources that spread towards the wall.
%
%  2. For each column we look at the nearest non‑wall cell to the wall.
%     Let d(C) be that distance and let v(C) be the value of the cell.
%     Among all columns we find:
%        * the smallest distance G = min_C d(C)  (global minimal distance)
%        * the largest value V among the columns whose distance equals G.
%
%  3. Columns are classified:
%        • HIGH   – d(C)=G  and  v(C)=V   (the highest value at the
%          global minimal distance)
%        • LOW    – d(C)=G  and  v(C)<V   (lower value at the global
%          minimal distance)
%        • OTHER  – d(C)>G
%
%  4. Colour spreading:
%        – HIGH columns:   the value v(C) is written in every cell
%          that lies between the source cell and the wall (inward).
%        – LOW columns:    only the cell *one step* away from the source,
%          on the side opposite the wall, receives the value v(C) (outward).
%        – OTHER columns:  the value v(C) is written inward, exactly as in
%          the HIGH case.
%        – All original non‑zero cells keep their colour.
%        – Wall cells (value = wall value) are never changed.
%
% -------------------------------------------------

% -------------------------------------------------
%  1. Identify the wall (full row of a colour)
% -------------------------------------------------
full_row(R,V) :-
    #count{C : input(R,C,V)} = #count{C : input(R,C,_)}.

wall_row(R) :-
    exists V, full_row(R,V), V != 0,
    not exists R2,V2, full_row(R2,V2), V2 != 0, R2 < R.

wall_value(V) :-
    exists R, wall_row(R), input(R,0,V).   % any column works for the whole row

% -------------------------------------------------
%  2. Distances of non‑wall non‑zero cells
% -------------------------------------------------
cellDistAbove(R,C,V,D) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 0, V != wall_value,
    R >= wall_row, D = R - wall_row.

cellDistBelow(R,C,V,D) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 0, V != wall_value,
    R <= wall_row, D = wall_row - R.

cellDist(R,C,V,D) :-
    cellDistAbove(R,C,V,D).
cellDist(R,C,V,D) :-
    cellDistBelow(R,C,V,D).

% -------------------------------------------------
%  3. Minimal distance per column and the best (highest) cell
% -------------------------------------------------
colDist(C,Dcol) :-
    cellDist(R1,C,V1,Dcol),
    not exists(R2,V2,d2), cellDist(R2,C,V2,d2), d2 < Dcol.

bestCell(C,R,V) :-
    colDist(C,Dcol), cellDist(R,C,V,Dcol),
    not exists(R2,V2,d2), cellDist(R2,C,V2,d2), V2 > V.

% -------------------------------------------------
%  4. Global minimal distance and maximal value among those columns
% -------------------------------------------------
global_min_dist(GD) :-
    colDist(C,GD), not exists(C2,D2), colDist(C2,D2), D2 < GD.

max_val(Vmax) :-
    bestCell(C,R,V), colDist(C,GD), max_val(V2), V2 > V.

% -------------------------------------------------
%  5. Column classification
% -------------------------------------------------
low(C) :-
    colDist(C,Dcol), global_min_dist(Dcol),
    bestCell(C,R,V), bestCell(C2,R2,V2), colDist(C2,Dcol), V2 > V.

source_above(C) :- bestCell(C,R,V), R < wall_row.

% -------------------------------------------------
%  6. Limits of the grid
% -------------------------------------------------
total_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_)}.
total_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_,C,_) }.

max_row(Rmax) :- Rmax = N - 1.
max_col(Cmax) :- Cmax = N - 1.

% -------------------------------------------------
%  7. Output generation
% -------------------------------------------------
% keep every original non‑zero cell unchanged
output(R,C,Vc) :- input(R,C,Vc), Vc != 0.

% outward neighbour for LOW columns
output(Rout,C,Vc) :-
    low(C), bestCell(C,R0,Vc), source_above(C),
    Rout = R0 - 1,
    Rout >= 0,
    input(Rout,C,0).

output(Rout,C,Vc) :-
    low(C), bestCell(C,R0,Vc), not source_above(C),
    Rout = R0 + 1,
    Rout <= max_row,
    input(Rout,C,0).

% inward filling for HIGH / OTHER columns
% (a column is *not* low => either distance > G or (d=G & v=Vmax))
inward(C) :- colDist(C,Dcol), bestCell(C,R0,Vc), not low(C).

output(R,C,Vc) :-
    inward(C), bestCell(C,R0,Vc), source_above(C),
    R = R0 + k,
    k >= 1,
    k <= wall_row - R0 - 1,
    input(R,C,0).

output(R,C,Vc) :-
    inward(C), bestCell(C,R0,Vc), not source_above(C),
    R = R0 - k,
    k >= 1,
    k <= R0 - wall_row - 1,
    input(R,C,0).

% -------------------------------------------------
%  End of program
% -------------------------------------------------
</asp>

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Transformation: “wall” of a full row with a non‑zero colour.
%  The colour of a source cell (the nearest non‑wall cell in a column)
%  spreads to all cells between that source and the wall.
%  Only the columns whose source is closest to the wall and whose
%  source colour is maximal among those columns are filled.
% -------------------------------------------------

% -------------------------------------------------
% 1. Grid dimensions
% -------------------------------------------------
total_rows(N) :- N = #count{R:input(R,_,_) }.
total_cols(M) :- M = #count{C:input(_,C,_)}.

% -------------------------------------------------
% 2. Wall: a row where every column has the same non‑zero colour
% -------------------------------------------------
wall_row(W), wall_val(Wv) :-
    #count{C:input(W,C,Wv)} = M,
    Wv != 0.

% -------------------------------------------------
% 3. Candidates: non‑wall non‑zero cells with their distance D
% -------------------------------------------------
candidate(C,R,V,D) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 0, R != W, V != wall_val,
    (R >= W, D = R - W).
candidate(C,R,V,D) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 0, R != W, V != wall_val,
    (R <  W, D = W - R).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 4. Choose the globally optimal source:
%    • minimal distance D,
%    • maximal value among those with the same D
% -------------------------------------------------
source(C,R,V,D) :-
    candidate(C,R,V,D).

% enforce “no better source” for the whole model
:- not (source(C2,R2,V2,D2), D2 < D).     % no source with a smaller distance
:- not (source(C3,R3,V3,D),  V3 > V).       % no source with same distance and larger colour

% -------------------------------------------------
% 5. Fill the interval between the source and the wall
% -------------------------------------------------
fill_above(C,R,V,Row) :-
    source(C,R,V,D),
    R < W,
    Row >= R+1,
    Row <= W-1,
    input(Row,C,0).

fill_below(C,R,V,Row) :-
    source(C,R,V,D),
    R > W,
    Row >= W+1,
    Row <= R-1,
    input(Row,C,0).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 6. Output rules
% -------------------------------------------------
output(Row,C,Val) :-
    fill_above(C,R,V,Row).

output(Row,C,Val) :-
    fill_below(C,R,V,Row).

output(Row,C,Val) :-
    input(Row,C,Val), Val != 0.

output(Row,C,0) :-
    input(Row,C,0).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 7. Zeros that are inside a filling interval must not be 0
% -------------------------------------------------
fill_interval(C,Row) :-
    fill_above(C,R,V,Row).
fill_interval(C,Row) :-
    fill_below(C,R,V,Row).

:- output(Row,C,0), fill_interval(C,Row).

% -------------------------------------------------
% 8. Exactly one colour per cell
% -------------------------------------------------
output_cell(R,C) :- true.
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

candidate_dist_below(R,C,V,D) :-
    candidate(R,C,V), R < wall_row, D = wall_row - R.

candidate_dist(R,C,V,D) :-

candidate_dist(R,C,V,D) :-

%  Transformation rule for the given examples
%  -------------------------------------------------
%
%  1. The whole grid contains a “wall” – a row that is filled
%     with the same non‑zero colour (the value 5 in the examples).

%     sources that spread towards the wall.

%  2. For each column we look at the nearest non‑wall cell to the wall.
%     Let d(C) be that distance and let v(C) be the value of the cell.
%     Among all columns we find:
%        * the smallest distance G = min_C d(C)  (global minimal distance)
%        * the largest value V among the columns whose distance equals G.
%

%        • HIGH   – d(C)=G  and  v(C)=V   (the highest value at the
%          global minimal distance)
%        • LOW    – d(C)=G  and  v(C)<V   (lower value at the global
%          minimal distance)
%        • OTHER  – d(C)>G

%        – HIGH columns:   the value v(C) is written in every cell
%          that lies between the source cell and the wall (inward).
%        – LOW columns:    only the cell *one step* away from the source,
%          on the side opposite the wall, receives the value v(C) (outward).
%        – OTHER columns:  the value v(C) is written inward, exactly as in
%          the HIGH case.
%        – All original non‑zero cells keep their colour.
%        – Wall cells (value = wall value) are never changed.
%
% -------------------------------------------------

%  1. Identify the wall (full row of a colour)
% -------------------------------------------------
full_row(R,V) :-

wall_row(R) :-
    exists V, full_row(R,V), V != 0,
    not exists R2,V2, full_row(R2,V2), V2 != 0, R2 < R.

cellDistBelow(R,C,V,D) :-

cellDist(R,C,V,D) :-

% Grid dimensions
total_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_)}.
total_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_,C,_) }.

% Wall row of constant non-zero colour
wall_row(W), wall_val(Vw) :-
    total_rows(N), total_cols(M),
    #count{C : input(W, C, Vw)} = M,
    Vw != 0.

% Candidate source cells (non-zero, not wall) with distance to wall
candidate(C,R,V,D) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 0, V != wall_val,
    (R >= wall_row, D = R - wall_row).
candidate(C,R,V,D) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 0, V != wall_val,
    (R < wall_row, D = wall_row - R).

% Source cell in its column: nearest distance, highest colour among those at that distance
source_candidate(R,C,V,D) :-
    candidate(C,R,V,D),
    not exists(C2,R2,V2,D2) : candidate(C2,R2,V2,D2), D2 < D,
    not exists(C2,R2,V2,D2) : candidate(C2,R2,V2,D2), D = D2, V2 > V.

% Guess global minimal distance and maximal colour among candidates at that distance
guessed_g(G) :- true.
guessed_vmax(Vmax) :- true.

% Ensure G is the minimal distance among source cells
:- source_candidate(R1,C1,V1,D1), D1 < G.

% Ensure there is a source cell at distance G
:- source_candidate(R2,C2,V2,G).

% Ensure Vmax is the maximum colour among source cells at distance G
:- source_candidate(R3,C3,V3,G), V3 > Vmax.

% Ensure there exists a source cell at distance G with colour Vmax
:- source_candidate(R4,C4,V4,G), V4 = Vmax.

% Column classifications
is_high(C,R,V) :- source_candidate(R,C,V,D), guessed_g(G), guessed_vmax(Vmax), D = G, V = Vmax.
is_low(C,R,V) :- source_candidate(R,C,V,D), guessed_g(G), guessed_vmax(Vmax), D = G, V < Vmax.

% Helper for distance comparison
distance_greater(R,C,V,G) :- source_candidate(R,C,V,D), D > G.

% Max row / column indices
max_row(Rmax) :- total_rows(N), Rmax = N - 1.

% Fill the interval between source and wall for HIGH columns
high_interval_cell(R,C,Vsrc) :-
    is_high(C,Rsrc,Vsrc),
    source_candidate(Rsrc,C,Vsrc,Dsrc),
    (Rsrc < wall_row, R >= Rsrc+1, R <= wall_row-1, input(R,C,0), V = Vsrc).
high_interval_cell(R,C,Vsrc) :-
    is_high(C,Rsrc,Vsrc),
    source_candidate(Rsrc,C,Vsrc,Dsrc),
    (Rsrc > wall_row, R >= wall_row+1, R <= Rsrc-1, input(R,C,0), V = Vsrc).

% Outward step for LOW columns (one cell opposite the wall)
low_outward_cell(R,C,Vsrc) :-
    is_low(C,Rsrc,Vsrc),
    source_candidate(Rsrc,C,Vsrc,Dsrc),
    (Rsrc < wall_row, R = Rsrc-1, R >= 0, input(R,C,0), V = Vsrc).
low_outward_cell(R,C,Vsrc) :-
    is_low(C,Rsrc,Vsrc),
    source_candidate(Rsrc,C,Vsrc,Dsrc),
    (Rsrc > wall_row, R = Rsrc+1, R <= max_row, input(R,C,0), V = Vsrc).

% Cells that remain zero (not involved in any fill)
zero_cell(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,0),
    not is_wall(R),
    not source_candidate(R,C,_),
    not is_high(R,C,_),
    not is_low(R,C,_),
    not high_interval_cell(R,C,_),
    not low_outward_cell(R,C,_).

% Expected colour for each cell
is_wall(R,C,Vw) :- R = wall_row, input(R,C,Vw), Vw != 0.
expected(R,C,V) :- is_wall(R,C,V), V = wall_val.

expected(R,C,V) :- source_candidate(R,C,V,D),
    (is_high(C,R,V) ; is_low(C,R,V) ; distance_greater(C,R,V,G)).

expected(R,C,V) :- high_interval_cell(R,C,V).
expected(R,C,V) :- low_outward_cell(R,C,V).

expected(R,C,0) :- zero_cell(R,C), V = 0.

% Output cells
output_cell(R,C) :- true.
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color), expected(R,C,Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

%  Transformation rule for the given examples
%  -------------------------------------------------

%        * the largest value V among the columns whose distance equals G.

%          global minimal distance)

%          minimal distance)
%        • OTHER  – d(C)>G

%        – LOW columns:    only the cell *one step* away from the source,

%        – OTHER columns:  the value v(C) is written inward, exactly as in
%          the HIGH case.

%        – Wall cells (value = wall value) are never changed.
%
% -------------------------------------------------

% -------------------------------------------------

    #count{C : input(R,C,V)} = #count{C : input(R,C,_)}.

    exists V, full_row(R,V), V != 0,
    not exists R2,V2, full_row(R2,V2), V2 != 0, R2 < R.
